title: Russia continues its attacks on power facilities in Kyiv as temperatures drop ahead of winter
summary: Russian forces hammered energy infrastructure around Ukraine's capital with missiles and drones overnight, straining Kyiv's power supply and heating systems as temperatures headed toward zero,…

image.caption: Firefighters work at the site of a Russian missile attack in Kyiv on Saturday. (Gleb Garanich/Reuters)

blocks.text: Russian forces hammered energy infrastructure around Ukraine's capital with missiles and drones overnight, straining Kyiv's power supply and heating systems as temperatures headed toward zero, officials said on Saturday.
Explosions rocked the capital as Russia fired multiple waves of ballistic missiles
Explosions rocked the city as Russia fired multiple waves of ballistic missiles, several of which hit and damaged the Northern Bridge across the Dnipro River, Mayor Vitali Klitschko.
Strikes on energy facilities outside Kyiv — including systems sending power from two nuclear plants to the city and Ukraine's central regions — caused serious damage, the Ministry of Energy said.
What can Canadian defence firms learn from Ukraine's drone expertise?

"The capital is facing serious difficulties with its electricity, water, and heat supplies," President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on social media platform X, adding that substations in five other regions were also hit.
He said Russia launched 36 ballistic missiles, only four of which were intercepted, according to Ukraine's air force. It added that air defences had downed 149 out of 172 drones.
At least two people were killed and about a dozen others wounded across Ukraine in the overnight attacks, which also damaged homes, businesses and non-residential buildings, authorities said.

Moscow's Defence Ministry said it carried out a massive strike on what it described as targets in Ukraine's military-industrial sector, as well as energy and transport infrastructure in and around Kyiv.

blocks.text: Russia has stepped up air attacks on Ukraine as its ground offensive has largely stalled, pounding energy infrastructure in major cities with difficult-to-intercept missiles and drones almost five years into its full-scale invasion.
It has expanded its campaign in recent weeks to target Kyiv's bridges, snarling traffic in the city of more than three million people.
B.C. animal rescuer killed by drone on Ukraine's front lines
Saturday's strikes come days before a new round of three-way talks in Abu Dhabi between Ukrainian and Russian officials, as part of a U.S.-backed peace push that has so far yielded few results.
"Russia is preparing for trilateral talks by launching ballistic missiles at Ukraine's critical infrastructure," Zelenskyy said on X.

blocks.text: The attacks also follow this week's U.S. midterm elections that have raised hopes in Ukraine for stronger support against Russia's war from a Democratic-controlled Congress.
"We are counting on the U.S. Congress to give more attention to Ukraine, because Russia keeps increasing the number of its attacks," Zelenskyy said.
